title: Introduce atomic release sequencer and restore verifier for safer private upgrades
author: Marisol Vega
release_notes: Adds an "atomic release sequencer" wrapper for helm upgrades, a post-restore verifier that runs cluster invariants and lightweight API probes, and a schema-migration dry-run mode for on-prem installs. No behavioral changes to default upgrade from an operator's perspective; opt-in behind feature flag.
body:
Motivation and summary: We have recurring incident post-upgrade where partially-applied helm/manifest sequences combined with out-of-order DB migrations lead to transient data/state mismatches and manual rollbacks. This PR introduces two complementary automation pieces that reduce human error and make upgrade/restore operations more deterministic for Private deployments: 1) an 'atomic release sequencer' binary (and Helm wrapper) that orchestrates small, ordered release changes with transactional checkpoints, and 2) a 'restore verifier' that runs post-restore sanity checks (CR status, schema fingerprints, KV-store checksums, and a small application-level probe) before marking the restore as complete.

What changed (high level): - New cli/tool: installer-sequencer (Go) that wraps helm upgrade/install and enforces a sequenced apply model. It records checkpoints to a namespace-scoped ConfigMap (immutable checkpoint IDs) and supports a --dry-run-preserve flag to stage operations into an ephemeral namespace for validation. - Helm chart changes: small hooks and a lightweight post-install probe container added to redwood-core chart; added labels/annotations used by the sequencer to detect release phases. - Restore verifier: a new step in the installer restore flow that validates: (a) DB migration versions match expected schema fingerprint, (b) critical CRDs are in Ready state, (c) sample inference request returns expected 200 + schema shape, (d) blobstore checksum matches pre-backup manifest. Failing checks halt finalization and emit diagnostics. - Schema migration dry-run mode: migration runner can execute in a transactionally-isolated ephemeral DB (when available) and produce a migration report used by the verifier. - Operational docs: runbook + example commands added to docs/installer/restore-verifier.md. - Tests: unit tests for sequencer state machine and integration tests exercising restore verifier against a small on-cluster dev DB.

Files changed (high level): - cmd/installer-sequencer/main.go (new) - internal/sequencer/state.go (new) - charts/redwood-core/templates/probe-job.yaml (modified) - charts/redwood-core/values.yaml (modified) - installer/restore/verifier.go (new) - installer/restore/fixtures/expected-schema.json (new) - docs/installer/restore-verifier.md (new) - test/integration/restore-verifier/* (new tests) plus small build/test infra changes to CI matrix.

Commit summary (single-line per commit): - 1a2d3f: add sequencer CLI scaffold and basic state machine; - 2b3c4d: implement checkpoint persistence and rollback hooks; - 3c4d5e: wire sequencer into helm wrapper and add feature flag; - 4d5e6f: add restore verifier core checks and report format; - 5e6f7a: chart probe/job and values; - 6f7a8b: integration tests + docs and CI matrix update.

Testing and CI: - Local unit coverage added for sequencer state transitions. - Integration job runs in the GH actions matrix using k3s (fast) to validate restore verifier end-to-end. - One flaky e2e run was observed on CI (race on the probe job pod readiness); flakiness mitigated by a small readiness-wait loop and the check re-run (see commit 6f7a8b). Final CI status: all checks green on the merged commit.

Security/upgrade considerations: - The sequencer persists immutable checkpoint IDs; the ConfigMap used is namespaced and read-only to non-installer service accounts. We added RBAC entries for the sequencer service account; review recommended. - Restore verifier requires read access to Secrets/ConfigMaps containing migration fingerprints; access is limited and scoped.

Migration/runbook (short): - Opt-in via installer flag --use-atomic-sequencer (defaults to off for now). - To perform a safe upgrade: 1) installer-sequencer stage --release redwood-core --version vX.Y.Z --dry-run-preserve (validate ephemeral run output). 2) If dry-run OK, installer-sequencer apply --release redwood-core --version vX.Y.Z. 3) On failure, sequencer will attempt deterministic rollback to last checkpoint (logs to /var/log/installer-sequencer.log). - For restore: installer restore --backup-id id1234 (when sequencer enabled, restore verifier runs automatically and will fail the restore if invariants not met). Docs include remediation steps and commands to extract diagnostics.

Review thread highlights: - Liam: asked for stronger invariants for schema fingerprinting (we now compute a normalized column/type fingerprint and include migration runner report). - Sofia: requested RBAC audit and minimal SA rights, addressed in commit 3c4d5e and documented. - Arjun: asked for a non-destructive dry-run for customers without ephemeral DB; we added a conservative checksum-based dry-run path that verifies schema compatibility without applying migrations.

Release/rollout plan: - Feature is behind a flag for now. We plan a gradual opt-in for customers doing Private upgrades; the default will remain as-is until we've exercised it with a small group. - Follow-up items tracked in ENG-4890: add grafana dashboards for sequencer checkpoint latencies and a telemetry ping on sequencer outcome (success/failure/rollback).

Why this is different from previous work: Existing upgrade safety PRs focused on transactional DB migrations or backup format. This PR focuses on treating the full release as an ordered, checkpointed sequence and pairing that with a stronger post-restore verification step and a migration dry-run mode—reducing manual intervention surface area for on-prem operators.

Notes: - Maintainers: please pay attention to the small Helm hook added (probe-job). It should be tolerant to cluster-level scheduling delays. - Tests added are intentionally conservative; we want to catch ordering races early.

Merge info: Squash merge performed. Merge commit message: "installer: atomic release sequencer + restore verifier (ENG-4821)".
notes_for_ops: Opt-in feature flag --use-atomic-sequencer. ConfigMap checkpoints live in namespace <release>-installer-checkpoints. RBAC changes in charts/redwood-core/templates/rbac.yaml. See docs/installer/restore-verifier.md for runbook.
